lessonRef.subject: ready-for-life
lessonRef.unitTitle: Caring for Home and Shared Spaces
lessonRef.title: Explicit model: ten-minute reset

objective: Learners watch an adult model a ten-minute reset routine for one shared space, then run the same four-step routine (clear, sort, return, wipe) themselves in a different space within about ten minutes.
scenario: A trusted adult first walks the learner through a ten-minute reset of one shared space, narrating each of four steps out loud: clear the surfaces, sort items into keep-here or belongs-elsewhere, return the belongs-elsewhere items to their homes, and wipe down the cleared surface. The learner then times themselves running the same four steps in a second shared space.
safetyNotes: Use respectful, non-shaming language about the starting condition of either space.

simulationAlternative.description: If no second shared space is available to reset independently, the learner instead resets the same first space a second time on a different day, timing themselves and comparing their independent time against the adult-modeled time.

tasks.directions: Before the model, predict which of the four reset steps you think will take the most time in this space and why.

prompts.text: Name the step you predict will take longest and give one reason.

tasks.directions: Watch and help with the adult's ten-minute reset of the first space, naming which of the four steps is happening as you go.

prompts.text: I could name the current step (clear, sort, return, or wipe) at least three separate times.
I helped with at least one full step alongside the adult.
I noticed one item that didn't have an obvious 'home' to return to.

tasks.directions: Run the same four-step reset on your own in a second shared space, keeping to about ten minutes.

prompts.text: Which step took the longest for you, and was that the step you predicted in the warm-up?

tasks.directions: Compare the space before and after your reset.

prompts.text: What is one thing about the four-step order (clear, sort, return, wipe) that made the reset go faster than just cleaning without a set order?

remediation: If the learner skips the sort step and tries to clear-and-wipe in one motion, reteach with a smaller five-item practice pile, having them physically separate it into two piles (belongs here / belongs elsewhere) before touching anything else.
extension: Have the learner time a reset in a third, messier shared space and write down one change they'd make to the four-step order for a space that messy.
